name: binCounts
title: Fast element counting in non-overlapping bins

origin.description: Counts the number of elements in non-overlapping bins.
origin.usage: binCounts(x, idxs = NULL, bx, right = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector of K positions to be binned and counted.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: bx
arguments.text: A numeric vector of B + 1 ordered positions specifying the B > 0 bins [bx[1], bx[2]), [bx[2], bx[3]), ..., [bx[B], bx[B + 1]).

arguments.name: right
arguments.text: If TRUE, the bins are right-closed (left open), otherwise left-closed (right open).

origin.details: binCounts(x, bx, right = TRUE) gives equivalent results as rev(binCounts(-x, bx = rev(-bx), right = FALSE)), but is faster and more memory efficient. Missing values in x are ignored. Missing values in bx are not allowed and give an error.
origin.value: An integer vector of length B with non-negative integers.

translation.description: Counts the number of elements in non-overlapping bins.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A one-dimensional numeric vector of K positions to be binned and counted. Missing values are dropped.

arguments.name: bx
arguments.text: A numeric vector of B + 1 ordered break points. The bins are [bx[j], bx[j + 1]) when right is false.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A 1-based subscript selecting elements of x, with the same rules as R's x[idxs]. None keeps every element. Missing selections are dropped with the missing x values.

arguments.name: right
arguments.text: If True, the bins are right-closed and left-open, (bx[j], bx[j + 1]]. If False, they are left-closed and right-open, [bx[j], bx[j + 1]). The default is True.

translation.details: Counts come from the bincounts crate, a port of matrixStats src/binCounts.c. x is sorted before the bins are filled. A value that lands on a break is counted in the closed side of that break. Missing bx is an error, as is an unordered or infinite bx.
translation.value: A one-dimensional int32 array of length B with non-negative counts.
translation.example:
from matrixstats.bincounts import binCounts
import numpy as np

x = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0])
bx = np.arange(11)
binCounts(x, bx, right=True)
binCounts(x, bx, right=False)
